objective: Establish what the Pi package pi-codex-conversion does as a Codex provider for Pi, and whether it supports Codex's context_management system, gpt-reserve, auto-review/auto-approve and comparable Codex features.
scope: Maintainer question (verbatim): "I'd like to know whether pi-codex-conversion does context_management (the new system), gpt-reserve, auto-review/auto-approve, etc".

Find pi-codex-conversion from authoritative sources: its npm registry entry (registry.npmjs.org/pi-codex-conversion), its source repository and README, its latest version, publish date, license and maintenance activity. Read its source, not just the README, for each feature claim.

Define each named feature from OpenAI's own sources (the openai/codex repository, its docs and changelog, and the OpenAI API docs) before checking it: what Codex's new context_management system is (compaction or context editing in the Responses API or Codex CLI), what 'gpt-reserve' refers to (if no source defines that term, say so and give the closest real feature, such as a reserved output or context budget, with the source), and what Codex's auto-review and auto-approve are (approval modes, an automatic reviewer of commands or changes). Then state per feature whether pi-codex-conversion implements it, partly, or not, with file:line or URL evidence.

The 'etc': also cover the other Codex-specific behaviour a Codex provider for Pi would need or miss: ChatGPT-subscription OAuth versus API key, the Responses API and reasoning effort or summaries, encrypted reasoning carried across turns, prompt caching keys, Codex's tool formats (apply_patch, shell), parallel tool calls, web search, image input, and anything the package documents as unsupported.

Compare with what Pi itself already offers for OpenAI or Codex (the pinned Pi host is at /home/user/holyagent/node_modules/.bun/@earendil-works+pi-coding-agent@1.5.0+8980da4117b98cd5/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent and its dependencies; look for a built-in openai-codex or openai-responses provider), so the report says what the package adds over Pi's built-in support.

Note how HolyAgent would consume it: HolyAgent installs Pi packages at exact pins from packages/runtime/src/config/pi-packages.json and its provider code is under packages/runtime/src/pi and packages/integrations/pi/src; state whether the package fits that model (a Pi package with an extension or provider), with paths.
constraints: Read-only: change no files, make no git writes, write nothing under .git/ or .holyagent/.
Never run pi, start a Pi session or make a live model or OpenAI request; reading registries, repositories and documentation is fine.
Separate sourced facts (with URL or path:line and the date fetched) from inference, and give versions.
Report in under 600 words; put long excerpts in a file in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad and give its path.

criteria.text: Each named feature (context_management, gpt-reserve, auto-review, auto-approve) is defined from an OpenAI source and marked implemented, partial or absent in pi-codex-conversion with evidence
The other Codex-specific behaviours listed are each marked with evidence, and what the package adds over Pi's built-in support is stated
Package facts (version, date, license, maintenance, fit with HolyAgent's Pi package pins) are sourced
